what_this_is: TSUGI incident 2 (2026-09-20): the daily drift witness found the served agent card no longer verifying after two version bumps (0.4.8, 0.4.9) deployed without a re-sign. Shield rule R3 proposed resign_agent_card and rejected redeploy_pinned; the operator authorized with the Ed25519 operator key (trust anchor at https://gate.horizonshield.dev/keys/operator.json); the operator re-signed and redeployed through the guard; the witness measured 0 drift after. 12 records: 8 drift (7 no-drift kept as evidence of the normal state), proposal, authorization (signed), execution, verify.
how_to_verify: node: verifyChain(records, { operatorKeys: await fetchOperatorKeys('https://gate.horizonshield.dev') }) with recovery_verify.mjs 0.3.0; python: recovery_verify.verify_chain(records, operator_keys=fetch_operator_keys(origin)). Every record_sha256 recomputes from its canonical bytes. Asking for a witness quorum (witnessQuorum) honestly fails: no witness was drawn, the pool was empty.

records.diagnosis: [R3_signature_only] the live card does not verify and the committed source does not verify either (--source-verifies false): the card body was edited after it was signed. Re-sign the current body with a2a-card-sign, then redeploy through the guard.

rejected.why: redeploying a body the signature was not made over serves the same mismatch again

records.rollback: restore the previous CARD_SIGNATURE constant from git and redeploy
establishes: both the live card and the committed source fail verification, so the fault is in the source, not the deploy

that the repair has been authorized or executed
